core_scientific_boundary.original_problematic_wording: V2 established exactly why the extra diesel was created.
core_scientific_boundary.corrected_approved_wording: V2 provides timestep-level evidence identifying observed forecast-to-dispatch-to-storage/diesel pathways associated with the aggregate diesel difference. The experiment does not isolate the causal contribution of every individual pathway or forecast horizon.

mechanism_classifications.M1_diesel_commitment: B — STRONGLY SUPPORTED (fewer startups 178 vs 346, longer commitment 400 vs 346 steps, higher power 33.79 kW vs 10.0 kW)
mechanism_classifications.M2_battery_dispatch: A — DIRECTLY ESTABLISHED FOR THE OBSERVED TEMPORAL PATHWAY (SOC divergence precedes diesel divergence)
mechanism_classifications.M3_renewable_curtailment: A — DIRECTLY ESTABLISHED AT THE OBSERVED DISPATCH/EVENT LEVEL (curtailment during minimum-output commitment)
mechanism_classifications.M4_soc_positioning: A — DIRECTLY ESTABLISHED FOR THE OBSERVED TEMPORAL PATHWAY (early SOC positioning persists)
mechanism_classifications.M5_forecast_shape: B — STRONGLY SUPPORTED, NOT INDIVIDUALLY ISOLATED (multi-horizon vector shape differences drive k=1 decision divergence)
mechanism_classifications.M6_multi_pathway: B — STRONGLY SUPPORTED (sequential forecast -> SOC -> curtailment -> diesel commitment chain)
mechanism_classifications.M7_other_mechanisms: E — NOT IDENTIFIABLE FROM THE AVAILABLE EVIDENCE

wording_corrections.original_problematic_wording: Treatment induces additional diesel commitment and startup events.
wording_corrections.corrected_approved_wording: Treatment exhibited fewer diesel startup events (178 vs 346) but longer diesel-on duration (400 vs 346 timesteps) and higher average diesel power (33.79 kW vs 10.0 kW) across diesel-active timesteps.
wording_corrections.reason_for_correction: Raw CSV telemetry proves Treatment had 178 startups vs Control's 346 startups. Claiming Treatment induced additional startups was factually incorrect.

wording_corrections.original_problematic_wording: The battery definitively caused the diesel increase.
wording_corrections.corrected_approved_wording: The preserved timestep telemetry directly shows early divergence in battery dispatch and SOC trajectories that precedes later diesel divergence. The observed forecast/optimization difference is associated with the subsequent battery/SOC pathway.
wording_corrections.reason_for_correction: Removes unproven causal assertion while locking the directly established temporal ordering.
wording_corrections.evidence_classification: A — DIRECTLY ESTABLISHED FOR THE OBSERVED TEMPORAL PATHWAY

wording_corrections.corrected_approved_wording: The telemetry shows renewable curtailment occurring during periods in which diesel commitment/minimum-output constraints limited renewable absorption. This provides evidence for a downstream pathway connecting forecast-dependent dispatch to renewable curtailment.
wording_corrections.reason_for_correction: Qualifies curtailment attribution to active minimum-output physical constraints during generator commitment.
wording_corrections.evidence_classification: A — DIRECTLY ESTABLISHED AT THE OBSERVED DISPATCH/EVENT LEVEL

wording_corrections.original_problematic_wording: h=5..12 was proven to cause the diesel increase.
wording_corrections.corrected_approved_wording: The treatment and control forecast vectors differed in their multi-horizon shape before the H1 forecast divergence occurred, and the optimizer/dispatch trajectories subsequently diverged. This strongly supports involvement of forecast-horizon shape, but the individual causal contribution of specific horizons was not isolated by this experiment.
wording_corrections.reason_for_correction: V2 did not independently manipulate individual horizons. Multi-horizon involvement is strongly supported, but isolated horizon causality is un-isolated.
wording_corrections.evidence_classification: B — STRONGLY SUPPORTED, NOT INDIVIDUALLY ISOLATED

wording_corrections.original_problematic_wording: Treatment has higher fuel efficiency than Control.
wording_corrections.corrected_approved_wording: The differing implied kWh/L ratios (0.74 kWh/L for Control vs 2.10 kWh/L for Treatment) arise from the documented nonlinear/penalty-based fuel-consumption model F(P) = 5.0 + 0.00025*P + 6.0*I_startup and the different diesel operating regimes observed in control and treatment; they should not be interpreted as a conventional constant fuel efficiency.
wording_corrections.reason_for_correction: Clarifies that implied kWh/L ratios stem from startup/idle penalty dominance in Control (346 short 1h runs) vs high-power continuous runs in Treatment (400 steps at 33.79 kW).
wording_corrections.evidence_classification: A — FULLY EXPLAINED BY DOCUMENTED MODEL SEMANTICS

wording_corrections.original_problematic_wording: Positive group mean +21.64 L; Negative group mean -13.06 L.
wording_corrections.corrected_approved_wording: Positive origins (N=95) exhibit a subgroup mean paired difference of +36.0633 L/origin (contributing +19.8035 L to overall population mean); Negative origins (N=77) exhibit a subgroup mean paired difference of -21.4230 L/origin (contributing -9.5351 L to overall population mean). The overall population mean paired difference across all 173 origins is +10.2684 L/origin.
wording_corrections.reason_for_correction: Reconciles subgroup means (+36.06 L / -21.42 L) with population-weighted contributions (+19.80 L / -9.54 L) to eliminate arithmetic ambiguity.
wording_corrections.evidence_classification: A — FULLY EXPLAINED BY DOCUMENTED MODEL SEMANTICS
